{{Quote
|Our holy land calls on us. To journey up is our greatest task. Who are we to refuse? Guided by faith, we climb through flaming fields, across rolling moors, and up great gilded steps. All to reach that eternal, shining Citadel.
|[[Pilby]]
|Hr=SS
}}

<b>The Citadel</b> is the religious institution that governs [[Pharloom]] and the destination for the pilgrims of the kingdom. It is the main location of [[Act 2]] of <i>[[Hollow Knight: Silksong]]</i> and houses seven areas: [[Choral Chambers]], [[Cogwork Core]], [[Grand Gate]], [[High Halls]], [[Memorium]], [[Whispering Vaults]], and [[Whiteward]].

<div class="hidden">
{{Hr|SS}}
<center>{{Typography|type=h2|text=The Citadel}}</center>
Clicking an area will lead to that area's page.
{{SS Citadel Map}}</div>

== Description ==
[[File:Screenshot SS The Citadel 01.png|thumb|200px|Architecture of the Citadel]]
The Citadel sits in a large cavern at the top of Pharloom.<ref>[[Chapel Maid]]: <i>"The bugs of the Citadel, at the summit of our land. (...) Our kingdom is gripped by a curse. Its paths grow wild and dangerous, and though some still attempt the climb to the Citadel at its crest, none return to speak of what they see."</i></ref> Strong wind blows outside of its upper levels. In contrast with the rest of the kingdom, the city's structures are opulent and intricately sculpted, and its rooms are lavish and richly decorated. The bulk of the Citadel is made of metal and stone covered in gold.<ref name=shakrabilewater>[[Shakra]]: <i>"That Citadel's shadow falls heavy here. I can sense its horrid bulk besides. It is no surprise to see it choke these caverns dank and stagnant. That monstrosity of metal and stone cares not for the lands it consumes."</i></ref><ref>[[Jubilana]]: <i>"The memories of my pilgrimage have all faded now, but a life spent in the Citadel's golden halls was all I ever wished for."</i></ref><ref>[[Garmond]]: <i>"Beasts and fiends, all here are lost to that horrid Haunting! And out from this golden corpse it seeps to plague the good bugs of the land below."</i></ref><ref>Chapel Maid: <i>"So you're another pilgrim then? Scuttled out of the darkness to climb the great path and bow at its gilded peak?"</i></ref> It is described as being shining, holy, and eternal.<ref>[[Pilby]]: <i>"About to start your great journey to the holy Citadel up top?"</i></ref><ref>Pilby: <i>"Strange question to be asking of a pilgrim. Our holy land calls on us. To journey up is our greatest task. Who are we to refuse? Guided by faith, we climb through flaming fields, across rolling moors, and up great gilded steps. All to reach that eternal, shining Citadel."</i></ref> Most of its inhabitants are now dead,<ref>[[Hornet (Silksong)|Hornet]] dialogue with [[Sherma]]: <i>"Hold your gratitude, little one. The dead are stirring."</i></ref> with many areas covered in webs and some entrances barred with furniture. Nearly all of the remaining bugs are [[Haunting|haunted]] and roam the halls and chambers of the city, posing a danger to those who still retain their own minds.

The city's main entrance is through the [[Grand Gate]], a great gilded door which must be opened with music and song to open the way into the Citadel itself. A long bridge leads to a room with massive scales that can be moved up or down. The lift at the end of this room goes down into the [[Underworks]], while there used to be a passage that went into the [[Choral Chambers]] at the top of the scales room. The Choral Chambers was where most of the Citadel's [[The Choir|Choir]] used to sing and where many of the Citadel's facilities were located, such as a restaurant, a spa, and an entrance to a [[Whispering Vaults#Sub-area: The Stage|theatre]]. It also contains [[Grand Bellway]], the only [[Bellway]] station in the Citadel. The [[Ventrica]], a network of steam-propelled vessels moved through pipes, provide fast travel within the city.<ref name=ventrica>Hornet dialogue with Shakra: <i>"Within the halls of the Citadel, I encountered a means of travel new to me, a network of pipes traversed in vessels propelled by steam and air."</i></ref> However, they were shut down due to a high number of injuries and unsanctioned deaths,<ref name=terminus>[[The Cradle#Terminus|Terminus]] [[Lore Tablets (Silksong)#The Cradle|Lore Tablet]]: <i>"Due to unacceptably high injury and unsanctioned deaths, Ventrica travel shall henceforth be denied to all. For Pharloom eternal, a bug who serves must never die."</i></ref> and need to be reactivated again.

Within the centre of the Choral Chambers lies the heart of the city's sustained song, the [[Cogwork Core]], constructed by the [[Architects]] and inhabited by [[Architects#Cogwork Bugs|automatons]].<ref>[[Twelfth Architect]]: <i>"Are you still to c-c-climb our grand core, Bug-Red? Within you may marvel at the work of Architects, my own, and all those passed b-b-before."</i></ref><ref>Twelfth Architect: <i>"Impressive-industrious... eternal... You have seen a glimpse, Bug-Red, of us-s-s, how once we were. The minds of Architects inspired. What majesty we did create..."</i></ref><ref>Twelfth Architect: <i>"The core remains to sustain the song, but no more Architects to tend-toil or build anew."</i></ref> A lift in the Core's central chamber goes up to [[the Cradle]], which can be opened by learning and then playing all three parts of the [[Threefold Melody]]. Northwest of the Core is the High Halls, a bright area filled with waterfalls, basins, and fountains where the highest ranking members of the Choir used to convene. Northeast is the city's [[Memorium]], an arboretum dedicated to preserving Pharloom's flora and fauna. East of the Choral Chambers is the Whispering Vaults, a dusty and gloomy archive where the [[Keepers]] stored the Citadel's history and secrets. The Whiteward is located below the Choral Chambers, and was where the city's [[Surgeon]]s performed experiments with [[Silk]]. 

== History ==
<h3>Creation</h3>
The Citadel was devised by the [[Weavers]] as both a church and a cage to keep [[Grand Mother Silk]] trapped in slumber.<ref name=maskmaker>Hornet and [[Mask Maker (Silksong)|Mask Maker]] dialogue:<br><i>Hornet: "You speak of the Citadel? Its former function has failed, but I can still sense its purpose, some. It is church and cage both."<br>Mask Maker: "Aye. Devised by your ancestors that monstrosity, and their wicked, clever minds. A system, or a web they'd likely call it, a way to keep their mother sealed in slumber, and themselves free to lavish in their false rule."</i></ref> The prayers and song from the bugs of the city sustained the [[Higher Beings|higher being]]'s prison.<ref>Pontiff [[Needolin Locations#Whispering Vaults|Needolin dialogue]]: <i>"Damned bugs... We prayed a cage... We sang your chains... Divine Silk..."</i></ref> It was said that all sang as one in the Citadel, and anyone who came from the city was known to bring song with them.<ref>Sherma: <i>"Our faith never wavered, and now here awaits our glorious reward, the shining Citadel! Where all sing as one!"</i></ref><ref>[[Old Penitent]]: <i>"S... song, is it? You have brought song? You are of the Citadel, then? How... how many of you?"</i></ref> Most bugs of the Citadel, with the exception of the [[Conductors]], were oblivious to its true purpose.<ref>Mask Maker: <i>"Our mortal mob did once act some defiance, unawares maybe, but successful in part, goaded towards it by Weavers' will'n all."</i></ref><ref name=conductorballador>[[Conductor Ballador]]: <i>"Is our state so bare, pilgrim?... "By the will of the Conductors," we once boomed, and this Citadel shook at our decree. But the words... How hollow they echoed. The mantle of rule, claimed greedily from Pharloom's fading first children, those bitter Weavers... it was yoke, not crown. Now, in our Citadel's silence, we share their truth. Only one monarch's claws ever clutched this kingdom, though we raised our voices to cry otherwise. Would you see her, pilgrim? Up there at our Citadel's crown? Reach those heights we'd hoped to hide and bow before this land's true ruler."</i></ref> The pontiff of the Keepers, one of the few who learned the truth, fell silent as a result.<ref>[[Vaultkeeper Cardinius]]: <i>"Only our pontiff, lived long and low within our vault, they held the melody, jealously, covetously... A learning for the highest Vaultkeeper, and them alone. A truth they were told to have found... There in the dark. Something within the melody, or the words. Something to set them silent..."</i></ref> The Citadel was meant to be eternal, and thus "for Pharloom eternal" was a common phrase.<ref>[[Second Sentinel]]: <i>"Eternal, is the Citadel. Et-t-ternal, is the devotion of the sentinels."</i></ref><ref>Vaultkeeper Cardinius: <i>"Divine music... The soul of Pharloom eternal laid bare..."</i></ref><ref name=terminus/><ref>Twelfth Architect: <i>"To serve, for Pharloom eternal."</i></ref>

It likely took the lifetimes of many bugs to build the whole structure.<ref>[[Seth]]: <i>"This great structure... It would have taken the lifetimes of so many bugs to build it."</i></ref> In the past, the Citadel was made of only simple stone and was bare and unadorned.<ref>[[Pious Isamor]]: <i>"See... Citadel's simple stone, bare an... dorned. See h...ain our garb, how sparse o... meal. Know that... excess is sin!"</i></ref> Over time, it became known for its excess and its unending consumption.<ref>[[Choir Hornhead]] [[Hunter's Journal (Silksong)|Hunter's Journal]] entry: <i>"Did this one grow large thanks to the Citadel's excess, or was its formidable size the reason it ever survived to reach this place?"</i></ref><ref name=shakrabilewater/> The Citadel turned the caverns of Bilewater dank and stagnant and made its waters murky,<ref>[[Bilewater]] map description: <i>"Swamps born in the Citadel's shadow. There is evidence the waters here once ran clear."</i></ref> producing exhaust fumes and smog.<ref>[[Bloatroach]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Obese offshoot of Muckroaches, born of the Citadel's exhaust smog."</i></ref><ref>[[Phantom]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Mournful creature tasked alone to expel the Citadel's choking refuse."</i></ref>

<h3>Structure</h3>
[[File:Screenshot SS Threefold Melody 01.png|thumb|200px|Cogwork Statues depicting a Conductor, an Architect, and a Vaultkeeper]]
The upper caste of the Citadel consisted of the [[Conductors]], the [[Architects]], and the [[Keepers]]. The Conductors' role was to rule the Citadel and to guide Pharloom to greatness.<ref>[[Cogwork Statues]]: <i>"We would hear the melody of the Conductors, high in their gleaming towers. They bearing the heaviest mantle, who would guide our land ever on to greatness."</i></ref><ref name=conductorballador/> The Architects were tasked with creating the machinery and automatons of Pharloom, sustaining its walls, floors, and voice.<ref name=architectsvoice>Cogwork Statues: <i>"We would hear the song of the Architects, at the core of our Citadel. They who sustain our realm, its walls, its floors and its voice, even as others fall silent."</i></ref><ref>Twelfth Architect: <i>"I am an Architect. Only an Architect. To build-automate is not choice. It is our nature-directive-c-c-c-cage."</i></ref> The Keepers were responsible for delivering sermons and leading prayers, as well as preserving the kingdom's history and secrets.<ref>Cogwork Statues: <i>"We would hear the voice of the Keepers, within their grand vaults. They who guard our history, our prayers and our secrets, across the ages."</i></ref><ref>Vaultkeeper Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"High caste bug, responsible for delivering sermons and leading prayer for those beyond the walls of the Whispering Vaults."</i></ref> All three groups deferred to the Weavers, who were still effectively in charge of the entire kingdom before their departure from Pharloom.<ref name=conductorballador/><ref name=maskmaker/><ref>[[Rune Harp]]: <i>"Last words of the Weavers. "Sisters, spiders, the burden is passed. These simple bugs shall bear it full. Never to cease. Never to silence.""</i></ref> 

The Citadel used the services and labour of many bugs throughout Pharloom. They requested for [[Forge Daughter]] to craft items in the [[Deep Docks]], where workers were employed to mine [[Flintstone]] for use in the Citadel's forgings.<ref>Hornet and [[Forge Daughter]] dialogue:<br><i>Forge Daughter: "Sent from our Forgehome we were, at request of those holy bugs above."<br>Hornet: "The Citadel dwellers? The veiled bugs? They ordered you here?"<br>Forge Daughter: "Yes! An age ago that. Such is duty! We Forge Daughters live to hone the craft, and aid the line. By the Citadel’s patronage, and our long duty upon these docks, our Forgehome would swell in holy esteem."</i></ref><ref>Flintstone [[Materium]] entry: <i>"Long burning rock from the base of Pharloom. Mined and used by the Citadel in its forgings."</i></ref> Bugs of [[Greymoor]] were charged to cut and collect fallen dregs of Silk to return to the Citadel.<ref>[[Silk Snipper]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Scissor-wielding bug charged to cut and spool fallen dregs of Silk for return to the Citadel above."</i></ref> However, they never saw the Citadel for themselves.<ref>[[Thread Raker]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Theirs seems a sad, grueling task, serving their lifetime for a Citadel unseen."</i></ref> The bugs of the [[Underworks]] worked incessantly for the Citadel.<ref>[[Underpoke]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"They toiled incessantly for the Citadel, their shells bent and greyed, and now the kingdom’s curse means not even death can relieve them."</i></ref> It was promised to them that they would eventually be brought upwards into the Citadel and obtain a holy reward.<ref>[[Loam]]: <i>"Me see you now! So clean, so lively... Surely you did come from above! Me time has come at last! Me work is done. You come to bring me up! Up, up!"</i></ref><ref>Loam: <i>"And when us works enough, thems see it... Hrrr... thems see it, and us gets us holy reward..."</i></ref> The [[Underworkers]] saw the Citadel as a bright and holy place, with fresh water for all and with very clean air.<ref>Loam: <i>"The Citadel! Most miracle of a place, bright and holy! Fresh water for all, much as can drink! Air so clean, can see the great rooves above! When me thinks of Citadel above, me works hardest of all!"</i></ref> Underworkers could confess their sins to an automated system, which always declared them guilty of a grave sin and told them to work off-cycle without stopping to eat.<ref>Underworks confessional machine: <i>"You have confessed a sin most grave and must by works cleanse yourself. Return to your task and work off-cycle, neither eating nor supping until new-cycle begins. By the grace of Pharloom eternal, may you never tire. Toil, and be forgiven."</i></ref>

Certain powerful groups had interactions with the Citadel as well. The [[Order of the Pinstress]] trained the Citadel's military in combat. The Citadel then turned that training against the Pinstresses, easily overwhelming them with their superior numbers until only two Pinstresses remained.<ref>[[Pinstress]]: <i>"Our grand Citadel learnt well from the training of Pinstresses past. Then it went and turned those teachings upon us! Despite our superior skills, our numbers have always been few, and their strength overwhelmed. Of my once revered order, only two of us remain, wormed away in Pharloom's forgotten corners, and my pin-sibling, she's lost herself to more peaceable pursuits."</i></ref> The Citadel also made a grudging accord with [[Nyleth]] of [[Shellwood]], building a shrine to her and sending their servants in reverence.<ref>[[Snail Shamans (Silksong)|Snail Shamans]]: <i>"We'd heard the Citadel once made grudging accord with that creature, sent their servants in reverence, even built a shrine up there somewhere. Maybe it's worth you searching for it?"</i></ref> Lastly, one of the princes of [[Verdania]] traded his soul and shell to become the mould for the [[Cogwork Dancers]] to keep his lands safe.<ref>[[Green Prince]]: <i>"The dancers... they were the last free act of my partner... Always hopeful. Always naive. His whole he gave, in desperate trade to see our own caves left safe. His shell and soul became the mould."</i></ref>

<h3> Sins </h3>
A major part of the Citadel's religious system was its focus on sins. Song always had to be sung, and none were allowed to falter in this.<ref name=ward>[[Whiteward]] [[Lore Tablets (Silksong)#Whiteward|Lore Tablet]]: <i>"While song must be sung, none may falter. Infirmity. Sickness. Death. All are banished from our Citadel."</i></ref> Infirmity, sickness, and even death were banished from the Citadel.<ref name=ward/><ref name=terminus/> Becoming infirm or sick was therefore seen as a sin.<ref>[[The Slab]] [[Lore Tablets (Silksong)#The Slab|Lore Tablet]]: <i>"Guilty of the sins of infirmity, sickness."</i></ref> Those who died after a Silk suture and refused to revive had also committed a sin, and their bodies were subsequently burned without rites.<ref>[[Choral Commandment]]: <i>"Devout has succumbed during Silk suture. Refuses to revive. Sin committed. Permit no rites. Husk marked for cremation. Retrieve dregs"</i></ref> Other sins were irreverence, dissonance, and apostasy.<ref>The Slab Lore Tablets: <i>"Guilty of the sin of irreverence.<br>Guilty of the sin of dissonance.<br>Guilty of the sin of apostasy."</i></ref>
[[File:Screenshot SS Old Penitent.png|thumb|200px|Penitent locked up in the Slab]]
Sinners were imprisoned in [[the Slab]],<ref>Hornet dialogue with Old Penitent: <i>"You needn't satisfy my curiosity if it pains you, sir, but I must ask, for what crime or sin did the Citadel imprison you?"</i></ref> where they could do penance in various ways, such as by being chained, swallowed, cast, or silenced.<ref>The Slab Lore Tablets: <i>"Penance by chaining.<br>Penance by silencing.<br>Penance by swallowing.<br>Penance by casting."</i></ref> Absolution was usually granted only after death, or not granted at all.<ref>The Slab Lore Tablets: <i>"Absolution granted after death.<br>Absolution not granted."</i></ref> The Slab's [[Slab Penitents#Jailers|jailers]]' ancestors had committed a sin against the Citadel. This sin had been so grave that their descendants had to serve in the Slab to obtain absolution.<ref>Hornet and Old Penitent dialogue:<br><i>Hornet: "Will you tell me of those who guard this structure? They are servants of the Citadel, are they not?"<br>Old Penitent: "Servants...? They too are penitents. In a past age, that caste committed their own sacrilege against the Citadel. A sin long forgotten, but so grave that their offspring and the offspring of their offspring carry the guilt with them still. To serve here is their only hope of absolution."</i></ref> [[Slab Penitents#Penitents|Penitents]] did not see the Slab as a prison, but as a holy place of forgiveness.<ref>Old Penitent: <i>P... prisoner? I understand you not. There is no prison here. This is a holy place of forgiveness. Please, speak with reverence."</i></ref> 

<h3>Technology</h3>
The Citadel had significant technological capabilities, with most of its technology crafted by the Architects and based on the standards of that of the Weavers.<ref>Twelfth Architect: <i>"An Architect’s work owes much to the art of the f-f-first children. They set expert standard for the tools and talents of Pharloom eternal."</i></ref> They used cogs and mechanisms for most of their machines, sometimes in combination with Silk, like for their [[Architects#Cogwork Bugs|cogwork automatons]].<ref>[[Cogwork Choirbug]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Bug forged of iron, rotor and cog."</i></ref> Early automatons of the Citadel required extensive Silk to maintain their function.<ref>[[Clawmaiden]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Puppet servant of the Citadel, suspended on strings of Silk. An early form of automaton, requiring extensive Silk to maintain its service."</i></ref> Tools like the [[Reserve Bind]] and the [[Spool Extender]] were focused on storing Silk.<ref>[[Reserve Bind]] description: <i>"Ornate artefact of the Citadel, able to hold a Bind's worth of Silk. Used when healing is needed and one’s natural resources run low."</i></ref><ref>[[Spool Extender]] description: <i>"Silk-storing tool of the Citadel, fashioned after an artefact of the Weavers."</i></ref> The Surgeons of the Whiteward used Silk to prolong life within the Citadel.<ref>[[Surgeon]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Their procedures with Silk may have prolonged life within the Citadel, but they unknowingly gifted many minds to the monarch."</i></ref> Non-Silk technology included metallic [[Psalm Cylinder]]s, which were etched with a recording of sound and could be played in a gramophone.<ref>[[Psalm Cylinder]] description: <i>"Metallic cylinder of Citadel make, etched with a recording of sound. The cylinder can be played in a gramophone."</i></ref> The Ventrica network, consisting of pipes that could be traversed in vessels propelled by steam and air, was used for travel within the city.<ref name=ventrica/>

<h3>Fall</h3>
At some point, the Architects completed the Cogwork Core, enabling it to produce song eternally by playing massive [[Psalm Cylinder|cylinders]] etched with recordings.<ref name=lastedict>Choral Commandment: <i>"Last edict of the Conductors. "And lo, is eternity sustained. By Architect’s claw, we welcome that final form, of dial and rotor, and soul gladly given. The perfect, unfaltering voice.""</i></ref><ref name=architectsvoice/><ref>[[:File:Screenshot SS Cogwork Core 19.png|Screenshot]] of the cylinders in the Cogwork Core.</ref> This meant the Citadel no longer had to rely on the Choir to sing.<ref name=architectsentinels/> The Conductors issued their final edict, announcing that they could now sustain the Citadel's voice for eternity.<ref name=lastedict/> However, the physicians of the Whiteward had put Silk harvested from Grand Mother Silk inside many bugs throughout Pharloom, seeding Silk deep inside their shells for generations.<ref>Hornet and the Caretaker dialogue: <br><i>Hornet: "In the ward down below, I saw it clear, the hollowed husks, and the many torturous implements... machines to instill a bug with thread, that would see their life extended."<br>Caretaker: "Aye! That's it, in part! But there's more scale to it than all that. Just think of'em greedily shoving the Silk into their shells, the madness that overcame them, eternal life for mortal bugs! Then think on how long it's all gone on..."<br>Hornet: "...The children born of them, and all the pilgrims after... The Silk has seeded deep into this kingdom's shells, generations deep..."</i></ref><ref>Pharloom's Folly: <i>"They forget your heart, bound in slumber and servitude,"</i></ref><ref>[[:File:Cocoon Grand Mother Silk.png|Screenshot]] showing Grand Mother Silk's cocoon in the Cradle, strands of Silk leading out from it similar to a loom.</ref> This made the bugs of Pharloom easy prey for Grand Mother Silk's [[Haunting|haunted]] thread, which only had to seek for itself to reach them.<ref>Hornet dialogue with the Caretaker: <i>"No wonder Pharloom's bugs proved such easy prey for that haunted thread. It had only to seek for itself to reach them."</i></ref> The Haunting caused the Citadel to fall into ruin and silenced its voices.<ref>Hornet and the Caretaker dialogue: <br><i>Caretaker: "Have you done it yet, bellringer? Wriggled deep? Discovered the depths of obsession that brought this place so low?"<br>Hornet: "If you speak of this Citadel and its Silk, Caretaker, then yes, I now know the start of it."</i></ref><ref>[[Choral Chambers]] [[Needolin Locations#Choral Chambers|Needolin dialogue]]: <i>"...All our wealth... ...All our glory... ...All to end... like this? ...Beauty... faded..."</i></ref><ref>Hornet dialogue with the Second Sentinel: <i>"I had assumed as much. Yet look around you, gilded one. During your slumber, the Citadel has fallen, and its voices lay silent. This place is dead, or very nearly. Some would argue that standing guard over a kingdom's corpse is a foolish task, empty of meaning. I wonder then, will you still hold true to your charge?"</i></ref><ref>[[Trobbio]]: <i>"Let us enliven this Citadel lost to silence!"</i></ref> The city and its inhabitants were the first to fall to the Haunting, which has affected its halls for a long time.<ref>[[Choir Pouncer]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Once one of Pharloom's favoured bugs, and yet their domain and their shells would have been the first to fall to the Haunting."</i></ref><ref>Jubilana: <i>"A settlement? In these long-haunted halls?"</i></ref><ref>Hornet dialogue with Sherma: <i>"You must have seen now that the bugs of this Citadel are long fallen to the Haunting."</i></ref> 

The Citadel has now been lost for generations and is only a gilded tomb drowned in Silk dregs.<ref>Hornet dialogue with the Seamstress: <i>"I have ventured high, seen the Citadel and its state. That place is long lost... generations lost, a gilded tomb, drowned in Silk dregs. For its minions, so compelled in my capture, I now see clearly the source of their unity, and their strange strength... They are husks bound tight by the one who waits at its crest..."</i></ref> When [[Hornet (Silksong)|Hornet]] enters the kingdom, the Citadel's castes are all haunted, and Grand Mother Silk is stirring.<ref>Hornet dialogue with Grindle: <i>"The creature that haunts this place is stirring, little thief. The Citadel's caste now roam the halls."</i></ref><ref>Hornet and Garmond dialogue:<br><i>Garmond: "Beasts and fiends, all here are lost to that horrid Haunting! And out from this golden corpse it seeps to plague the good bugs of the land below. Well, no more we say!"<br>Hornet: "You should beware brave sirs, the creature that commands this curse is a foe far beyond bug."</i></ref> New pilgrims are kept safe once Hornet reawakens the bell of [[First Shrine]], which protects against the Citadel's dangers.<ref>Hornet dialogue with Jubilana: <i>"A small settlement has formed there, and the bell, reawakened, seems to ward away the worst of the Citadel's many dangers."</i></ref>

==Pilgrimage==
[[File:Screenshot SS Tall Pilgrim 01.png|thumb|200px|Pilgrims in front of the Grand Gate]]
Simple bugs are compelled to take on a pilgrimage to reach the Citadel at Pharloom's summit, as they feel that it calls them.<ref>Hornet and the [[Caretaker]] dialogue:<br><i>Hornet: "These poor bugs, all are victims of the Citadel and its insidious attraction. This place draws them up, into its maw, only to consume them, utterly."<br>Caretaker: "Aye, inside and out, s'nothing but a grand, gilded lie."</i></ref><ref>[[Aged Pilgrim]]: <i>"Might have taken me a beat to build the courage, but I can feel it, closer now... the Citadel calling me up."</i></ref><ref>Hornet dialogue with Pilby: <i>"Your life is your own, and need not be squandered at the ghostly call of the Citadel."</i></ref> The path is severely punishing, but pilgrims see it as a test.<ref name="mort">[[Mort]]: <i>"The lands in every direction punish us, but such is our test. Above it all, the Citadel shines, our destination and our reward... I'll make it there, you'll see. I've easily earned my place in such a paradise."</i></ref> Even with the kingdom's decline, the Citadel's grandeur still draws bugs to it.<ref>Chapel Maid: <i>"...It's that Citadel above, you see. Even now, in Pharloom's long decline, the simple bugs, they're witless before it. Too grand. Too majestic. Too powerful."</i></ref> The pilgrims believe it is a paradise, that it can heal all ails of their journey, and that a great reward awaits them at the end.<ref name="mort"/><ref>[[Exhausted Pilgrim]]: <i>"My sore shell will cease tormenting me once I reach the Citadel. It's sung that all ails are healed just as soon as we step beyond the Grand Gate..."</i></ref> Most pilgrims leave for the Citadel soon after arriving in Pharloom.<ref>Hornet dialogue with Shakra: <i>"The pilgrims here seem to have no mind for war, Shakra. I suspect most depart for the Citadel soon after their arrival."</i></ref>

Pilgrims are required to venture through the lower areas of Pharloom in order to make sure the five bells in the [[Bellshrine]]s are rung.<ref>Hornet and [[Tall Pilgrim]] dialogue:<br><i>Hornet: "I have passed several such bells, pilgrim. I know how to see them woken. Tell me what you know of their locations, and I shall seek those that still remain silent."<br>Tall Pilgrim: "Sister? This is a mighty service you willingly perform! What a marvellous gift you would grant to your fellows. Eagerly, I shall tell you of the shrines and their locations, as we have heard them spoken..."</i></ref> The bells at the [[Grand Gate]] then have to be attuned with music, allowing them access to the Citadel.<ref>Tall Pilgrim: <i>"The bells are rung? Then this sacred threshold may now be crossed, for the final task is simple! Only music, played fair and true. Music shall attune the bells, and see the gate descend."</i></ref> The final hurdle to reach the gate is the ascension through the [[Blasted Steps]], where pilgrims judged to be sinful are killed by the [[Judges]].<ref>[[Judge]] Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"They remorselessly eliminate any pilgrim or passerby deemed impure to their sight."</i></ref><ref>Last Judge Needolin dialogue: <i>"Only the pure may pass! Smite the sinners!"</i></ref> Pilgrims are not allowed to arm themselves with weapons, having to rely on their prayer and faith to reach the Citadel.<ref>[[Horned Pilgrim]] and Hornet dialogue:<br><i>Hornet: "I strongly suggest you arm yourself similarly before your own journey begins."<br>Horned Pilgrim: "Alas... for a pilgrim, that's sin you speak of, sister. We arm ourselves with prayer, garb ourselves in faith, and hope they prove enough to reach the Citadel's glory. Such is our way..."</i></ref> In the past, before the creation of the Cogwork Core, the [[Second Sentinel|sentinels]] protected the pilgrims and forced some bugs to go to the Citadel to serve.<ref>Second Sentinel: <i>"D-defence of the sacred Citadel, and the voices that fill it-t-t, is the eternal duty of the sentinels."</i></ref><ref name=architectsentinels>Twelfth Architect: <i>"Long before the c-c-creation of the core, the sentinels ventured, even beyond these walls, to see all bugs brought-forced safe to serve the Citadel."</i></ref> 

Most pilgrims that were admitted to the Citadel were inducted into the Choir and were gifted a [[Choir Cloak]],<ref>Choir Pouncer Hunter's Journal entry: <i>"Agile bug, and one of few hardy pilgrims to have reached the Citadel."</i></ref><ref>[[Choir Cloak]] description: <i>"Garment gifted to pilgrims on admittance to the Citadel. Its thick weave offers additional protection against wind and cold."</i></ref> while other pilgrims were sent to the Underworks to work there.<ref>Loam: <i>"Hrrrrr? Hrrrrrr. You speaks strange. Me can not rest. Us works, and Citadel breathes, and thems above do sing, and all is right."</i></ref><ref> [[Bone Scroll]]: <i>"So much suffering. Are we truly chosen, or have we sinned unknowing, and now are punished for it?"</i></ref> To end their pilgrimages, the worthiest of the pilgrims were supposedly chosen to ascend to the Cradle to worship before the kingdom's divine heart.<ref>[[Grand Reed]] Needolin dialogue: <i>"Those worthiest may climb... The holy heights of the Citadel... May my voice never fade... May my shell never break... For my devotion... unending... May I rise... May I rise..."</i></ref> To be allowed to ascend, pilgrims had to obtain the Threefold Melody, which included a climb that was never intended for regular bugs.<ref>Cogwork Statues: <i>"Pilgrim of Pharloom eternal, you rare chosen who hath ascended to this final threshold, listen to our wish, deliver it, that you may rise above and see your pilgrimage end. (...) Pilgrim of Pharloom eternal, regale us with our Threefold song, that you may rise above and worship before our kingdom's divine heart."</i></ref><ref>Hornet dialogue with Twelfth Architect: <i>"I have, maker. Clearly it was a climb never intended for regular bugs, and fair fortune that the skills gifted within your lands allowed my ascent."</i></ref> The Keepers' part of the melody was also never meant to be given to a bug who was not a Keeper.<ref>Vaultkeeper Cardinius: <i>"Our pontiff's sacred cylinder, stolen from the dark below... Never! States our law. Never must our melody pass to a bug not Keeper!"</i></ref>

== How to Access ==
The Citadel can be first accessed from the [[Blasted Steps]] after defeating the [[Last Judge]], who guards the [[Grand Gate]]. The path from the Grand Gate leads to the [[Underworks]] and then to the [[Choral Chambers]]. It can also be first accessed from [[Bilewater]] after defeating [[Phantom]] in [[Exhaust Organ]]. This path goes through a small part of the Underworks and ends at Grand Bellway in the Choral Chambers.
